files.title: Digital Omnibus on data: GDPR, ePrivacy, Data Act, NIS2
files.status: The Commission proposed it on 19 November 2025. The Council has no negotiating position yet: EU ambassadors were due to agree one on 7 October 2026, but the item was postponed, and their 11 October meeting did not take up the Irish Presidency's compromise (Agence Europe). Parliament's position is still being built in joint ITRE-LIBE work and will take months. Open fights: personal data and pseudonymisation, AI training on personal data, trade secrets under the Data Act, and whether cookie rules move into the GDPR or stay in ePrivacy.

files.title: Digital Networks Act
files.status: Proposed 21 January 2026. It replaces the EECC, BEREC regulation and Radio Spectrum Policy Programme and extends authorisation rules to cloud providers and CDNs. The Council issued a progress report on 2 June 2026, and telecoms ministers discussed the act at their informal meeting in Limerick on 12–13 October. The Irish Presidency aims to present a progress report at the Telecoms Council on 1 December. IMCO and LIBE draft opinions were published in June.

files.title: Digital Fairness Act (and a possible EU social media minimum age)
files.status: The Commission's indicative planning of 29 September lists the proposal for 11 November 2026, in a consumer package; the date can still move. Expected themes: dark patterns, addictive design, influencer marketing, unfair personalisation and minors. A bloc-wide social media minimum age may come alongside or inside it. Member States are moving first, for example Denmark's consultation on a minimum age of 15 launched 7 September 2026.

files.title: Technology Sovereignty Package: Chips Act 2.0 and Cloud and AI Development Act
files.status: The Commission proposed both on 3 June 2026. In Parliament, ITRE leads the Chips Act 2.0 (rapporteur Oliver Schenk) and ITRE and IMCO share the CADA (Diego Solier and Reinier van Lanschot). The Council's industry working party resumed talks on the Chips Act 2.0 on 2 September 2026 and met on it again on 12 and 13 October. The CADA aims to triple EU data-centre capacity within five to seven years and creates a framework to assess cloud and AI sovereignty, which is the most contested element.

files.title: AI Act implementation after the Digital Omnibus on AI
files.status: The Digital Omnibus on AI entered into force on 27 July 2026. Annex III high-risk obligations now apply from 2 December 2027 and Annex I from 2 August 2028. Providers of generative AI already on the market have until 2 December 2026 for labelling measures. The live issues are standards, AI Office enforcement and national authority designation.
